public_sources.title: Sequential testing of conditionally constrained hypotheses
public_sources.author: Eugenio Clerico
public_sources.used_scope: For nulls defined by finitely many conditional constraints, every e-process is pointwise dominated by a predictable product of affine one-step e-variables. The paper explicitly frames predictable affine factors as a lossless action class for conditional sequential testing; limitation: finitely many constraints.

public_sources.title: Safe testing
public_sources.authors: Peter Grunwald; Rianne de Heide; Wouter Koolen
public_sources.used_scope: Conditional e-variables may be constructed just in time from all information available before the next outcome, including covariates, provided the conditional safety property holds; products then remain safe under optional continuation. The paper also warns that overlapping data cannot simply be multiplied as if fresh.

public_sources.title: Strong duality for the GROW criterion
public_sources.authors: Ashwin Ram; Martin Larsson; Johannes Ruf; Aaditya Ramdas
public_sources.used_scope: GROW gives a worst-case log-growth criterion against composite alternatives; bounded e-variables admit a general minimax strong-duality characterization. Used as theoretical support for treating transfer uncertainty as an explicit robust alternative set rather than a single point prediction.

public_sources.title: Time-sensitive anytime-valid testing
public_sources.authors: Eugenio Clerico; Tobias Wegel; Iskander Azangulov; Patrick Rebeschini
public_sources.used_scope: Finite-time utility and hard deadlines can favor policies different from asymptotic GRO; the optimal-control formulation depends on time and wealth, so worst-case log growth and reject-by-deadline utility should be measured separately.

covariate_conditioned_paired_sign_factor.setup: For task t let Z_t be task-side information observed before paired labels/outcomes. Encode X_t=+1 for candidate-only success, -1 for incumbent-only success, 0 for concordance. Under the conditional sign null require P(X_t=+1 | F_{t-1}, Z_t) <= P(X_t=-1 | F_{t-1}, Z_t).
covariate_conditioned_paired_sign_factor.factor: For any predictable b_t=b(F_{t-1},Z_t) in [0,1], e_t=1+b_t X_t is a conditional e-variable because E[e_t | F_{t-1},Z_t]=1+b_t(P(+)-P(-)) <= 1. Concordant tasks contribute factor 1. Equivalently q_bet=(1+b_t)/2 gives factors 2q_bet and 2(1-q_bet) on discordant signs.
covariate_conditioned_paired_sign_factor.consequence: Task difficulty, benchmark family, cost class, or other pre-outcome covariates may safely choose the next bet and can absorb arbitrarily dependent/predictable task ordering, provided the sign-null is itself asserted conditional on those covariates. The Clerico complete-class result implies that for finitely constrained conditional nulls, searching beyond predictable affine one-step factors cannot improve pointwise testing power.
covariate_conditioned_paired_sign_factor.scope_guard: This does not permit covariates computed from the fresh paired labels, post-outcome judge features, or task-selection signals that are descendants of the outcome being bet on. Nor does one candidate-level e-process solve multiplicity across an adaptive stream of candidates.

finite_map_robust_log_growth.setup: Two pre-outcome task strata: low/high with frequencies .5/.5 and discordance rates .2/.6. Consider three alternative transfer maps for discordant candidate-win probabilities: correct=(.60,.80), flat=(.70,.70), inverted=(.80,.60).
finite_map_robust_log_growth.minimax_grid: Maximizing the minimum expected per-task log growth over q_low,q_high in [0.5001,0.8999] yielded approximately q_low=.79254, q_high=.60986 with worst-case expected log growth .025236 nats/task; expected log growth was essentially equalized across all three maps.
finite_map_robust_log_growth.counterintuitive_result: The robust solution is not the pointwise middle map. Because the high stratum is three times more likely to be discordant, minimax hedging allocates the stronger bet to the low-discordance stratum and a weaker bet to the high-discordance stratum to equalize regret across possible transfer inversions.
finite_map_robust_log_growth.scope_guard: This is a stylized two-stratum finite alternative set, not a general formula for arbitrary task distributions. If the robust alternative set includes the null q=.5 itself, worst-case positive log growth collapses to zero and pure maximin becomes too conservative without an additional utility/regret criterion.

hierarchical_map_mixture.construction: Maintain three covariate-aware e-processes corresponding to the correct/flat/inverted transfer maps and average their wealth with protocol-fixed prior weights (equal weights in the stress test). This is a valid e-process because it is a fixed convex mixture of valid conditional e-processes; component wealth performs implicit posterior-like reweighting without post-hoc selecting the largest component.
hierarchical_map_mixture.interpretation: Bayes-style map mixtures and GROW-style worst-case bets optimize different objectives. The mixture retains substantial average power under uncertainty, whereas the maximin bet buys a much flatter worst-case rejection profile at the cost of short-horizon resolution.

worker_local_simulation.design: Monte Carlo paired-sign stream with threshold 1/alpha=20, alpha=.05. Task stratum high with probability .5; discordance rho_low=.2, rho_high=.6. Alternative maps correct=(q_low=.60,q_high=.80), flat=(.70,.70), inverted=(.80,.60). 60,000 trajectories per map/strategy/horizon; null checks 120,000 trajectories per horizon. Simulations are illustrative finite-grid stress tests, not external empirical evidence.

null_sanity.interpretation: All empirical crossing rates stayed below .05. The proof, not Monte Carlo, provides validity; the Markov difficulty check only catches implementation mistakes and illustrates that predictable dependence in task strata need not break a conditionally valid sign process.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Condition paired-sign validity on pre-outcome task covariates and choose each affine sign bet predictably from those covariates/history. Treat task difficulty as side information for bet allocation rather than as extra independent samples.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct conditional-expectation derivation; Safe Testing just-in-time conditional e-variable rule; Clerico 2026 complete-class theorem for finitely constrained conditional hypotheses.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Requires conditional sign-null after conditioning on every feature used to set the bet. Fresh labels/post-outcome features cannot enter before the factor is fixed.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Represent uncertainty in pre-audit-to-fresh transfer as a protocol-fixed mixture over several covariate-effect maps, then let fresh component wealth reweight them implicitly.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Convex-mixture e-process proof plus worker-local three-map stress test. At T=100 the map mixture had average reject-by-horizon .652 versus .644 for fixed q=.75, with worst-map .445 versus .421.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Short-horizon results reversed: at T=20 fixed q=.75 had higher average/worst rejection than the equal-weight mixture. Prior/map support must be tuned on disjoint meta-data or otherwise safely accounted for.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Choose covariate-specific sign bets by maximizing worst-case expected log growth over a prespecified transfer-map uncertainty set.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: GROW theory motivates the criterion; worker-local grid equalized expected log growth across three transfer maps and gave the strongest worst-map T=100 rejection (.518) among tested uncertainty-aware strategies, but very weak T=20 rejection (~.004).
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Worst-case asymptotic log growth is not the same objective as reject-by-deadline utility. Use only when the ambiguity set and long-horizon robustness objective are genuinely appropriate.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'shared task difficulty or predictable task ordering automatically invalidates paired-sign e-processes.' It need not: condition the sign null on pre-outcome covariates/history and use predictable affine factors. What matters is conditional validity, not i.i.d. task difficulty.

Rejected: 'a black-box complex e-process can exploit conditional task features better than predictable affine betting in this finite-constraint setting.' Clerico's complete-class result says every e-process is pointwise dominated by such a predictable affine product under the stated class.

Narrowed: 'minimax/GROW robustness is a safe default for short evaluation budgets.' In the stylized stress test it greatly reduced 20-task rejection despite strong worst-case 100-task behavior; finite-horizon utility must be evaluated separately.

Narrowed: 'Bayesian mixtures dominate fixed bets under model uncertainty.' Equal-weight map mixing improved the T=100 average and inverted-map performance but lost badly at T=20; mixture priors and deadline matter.

Rejected: 'any task feature can be used as side information.' Features influenced by the fresh labels/outcomes, post-hoc judge decisions, or outcome-adaptive task selection can violate the conditional sign constraint and must be gated out or explicitly modeled.

frontier.action: Derive a time-sensitive/minimax-regret policy for covariate-conditioned paired signs that optimizes reject-by-deadline or asymmetric harmful-commit utility over a transfer-map ambiguity set, rather than worst-case long-run log growth. Compare Bellman/REGROW-style policies with fixed convex map mixtures on 10-200 task horizons.

Introduce shared task difficulty across multiple candidate comparisons and formalize when current-task covariates are pre-outcome/predictable. Separate within-candidate conditional validity from run-level multiplicity under cross-candidate dependence; construct a counterexample where a post-outcome task feature breaks the e-process.

Move reused-development candidate evaluation from fixed-horizon e-values to actual anytime PACE paths. Include stopping time, running supremum and any returned metadata in the selectable transcript before applying selection/description-length corrections.

For repeated modification streams, compare run-level alpha spending, e-closed testing, and dependence-robust e-value multiple testing while keeping candidate-generation data adaptivity as a separate validity axis.

Build a disjoint-meta calibration protocol for transfer-map support/prior weights and report sensitivity to missing/inverted maps, task-family shift, discordance-rate shift, harmful-commit cost and unresolved decisions.

frontier.exact_next_action: Solve a finite-horizon robust control problem for covariate-conditioned paired-sign betting under a small transfer-map ambiguity set, with explicit harmful-commit/unresolved costs, then add a post-outcome-side-information counterexample to pin down the filtration boundary before moving to cross-candidate multiplicity.
